sourceNote.title: Login rate limiting
sourceNote.html:
Login rate limiting

Exploring the sign-in rate limit on a test environment with a throwaway account (tester@example.test).

  • After 5 failed passwords within 15 minutes for one account, sign-in is locked for 15 minutes.

  • The lock message says "Too many attempts. Try again in 15 minutes." and does not reveal whether the account exists.

  • A successful sign-in resets the failed-attempt counter.

  • Unknown email addresses get the same generic error and also count towards a per-IP limit of 20 attempts per 15 minutes.

  • Password reset link still works while locked.

  • Observed: the 5th failure already showed the lock message, so the 5th attempt might count as locked instead of the 6th.

  • Open question: does the lock apply per account across devices?

bodyHtml:
Feature: Login rate limiting

Coverage uses the test environment and throwaway account tester@example.test.

Scenario: Account lock threshold and duration

Test case: Lock after five failed passwords within 15 minutes

Purpose: Verify the account lock boundary, message, and duration.

Preconditions: Given the account is unlocked with no failed attempts in the current window.

Test data: tester@example.test; incorrect passwords; five failures within 15 minutes; the correct password for checking lock expiry.

Steps:

  1. When four incorrect passwords are submitted within 15 minutes, record the response after each attempt.

  2. When a fifth incorrect password is submitted within the same window, record whether that attempt displays the lock message.

  3. When sign-in is attempted during the 15-minute lock, record the response.

  4. When the 15-minute lock has elapsed, attempt sign-in with the correct password.

Expected result: Then five failed passwords trigger a 15-minute sign-in lock displaying “Too many attempts. Try again in 15 minutes.” Sign-in becomes available after the lock expires.

Coverage notes: The note observed the lock message on the fifth failure. Preserve whether the fifth attempt triggers and displays the lock or whether the message first appears on the sixth. Whether the lock applies to the same account across devices remains an open question.

Scenario: Successful sign-in resets failed attempts

Test case: Earlier failures do not carry over after success

Purpose: Verify that successful sign-in resets the failed-attempt counter.

Preconditions: Given tester@example.test is unlocked with a clear failed-attempt counter.

Test data: tester@example.test; incorrect passwords; the correct password.

Steps:

  1. When four failed sign-in attempts are made within 15 minutes, then sign in with the correct password.

  2. Return to sign-in and submit four more incorrect passwords within 15 minutes.

  3. Submit a fifth incorrect password after the successful sign-in.

Expected result: Then the successful sign-in clears the earlier failures. The next four failures do not trigger the account lock; the fifth failure after success triggers it.

Coverage notes: Covers reset behavior immediately below and at the five-failure threshold.

Scenario: Generic errors and the per-IP limit

Test case: Unknown email attempts remain generic and count toward the IP limit

Purpose: Verify account-existence privacy and inclusion of unknown email attempts in rate limiting.

Preconditions: Given a test IP has no attempts in its current 15-minute window, and unknown email addresses are available.

Test data: Unknown email addresses; tester@example.test for error comparison; incorrect passwords; 20 attempts from one IP within 15 minutes.

Steps:

  1. When an incorrect password is submitted for tester@example.test, record the generic error.

  2. From an IP with a clear attempt window, submit incorrect passwords for unknown email addresses and compare the error with the known-account response.

  3. Continue the unknown-email attempts from that IP to reach 20 within 15 minutes, recording responses around the limit.

  4. Attempt one additional sign-in within that window and record the response.

Expected result: Then unknown email addresses receive the same generic error without revealing whether an account exists. Those attempts count toward the per-IP limit of 20 attempts per 15 minutes.

Coverage notes: The note does not specify the per-IP limit response, its exact triggering attempt, or a way to inspect its counter. Record these observations; the precise boundary outcome needs clarification.

Scenario: Password reset remains available during lock

Test case: Use the password reset link while sign-in is locked

Purpose: Verify that the sign-in lock does not prevent use of the password reset link.

Preconditions: Given tester@example.test is within its 15-minute sign-in lock.

Test data: tester@example.test; the password reset link.

Steps:

  1. When sign-in is attempted, confirm that the lock message is displayed.

  2. While the lock is active, use the password reset link.

Expected result: Then the password reset link still works while sign-in is locked.

Coverage notes: The note does not define reset-flow details or whether resetting a password clears the lock.
